{"prompt": "I got a job offer for $95k but I was hoping for $110k. Help me write a counter-offer email.", "response": "Subject: Re: Offer for Senior Analyst — A Quick Follow-Up

Hi Priya,

Thank you again for the offer — I'm genuinely excited about the role and the team. Before I confirm, I wanted to discuss the compensation package.

Based on my research into market rates for this role and my six years of relevant experience in forecasting, I was hoping we could land closer to $110,000 base. I'm confident I can bring a lot of value from day one, and I'd love to find a number that works well for both sides.

Happy to hop on a call this week if that's easier.

Best,
Jordan"}
{"prompt": "Draft an email asking my landlord to reduce the rent increase from 12% to something more reasonable.", "response": "Subject: Regarding the Proposed Rent Increase

Hi Teresa,

Thank you for the renewal notice. I've valued being a reliable tenant here for three years and would like to continue, but a 12% increase is a significant jump above what I've seen for comparable units in the area (closer to 4-6%).

Would you be open to meeting somewhere in that range instead? I'm glad to sign a longer lease term if that helps make a smaller increase workable on your end.

I appreciate you considering this, and I'm happy to discuss further whenever works for you.

Best regards,
Alex"}
{"prompt": "I need to tell a client their project will be delayed by two weeks without losing their trust.", "response": "Subject: Project Timeline Update

Hi Renata,

I want to flag an update on our timeline as early as possible. We've hit an unexpected integration issue with the payments provider that will push our delivery date back by two weeks, to the 24th.

We're already adding an extra QA pass and reallocating a second engineer to prevent further slippage, and I'll send a short progress update next Monday so you're not waiting in the dark. I know timing matters on your end, and I take that seriously — happy to discuss any ways we can soften the impact on your side.

Thanks for your patience on this.

Sam"}

final_entries.prompt: A supplier just raised their prices by 18%. Help me negotiate them back down.
final_entries.response:
Subject: Price Adjustment Discussion — Q4 Contract

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the updated quote. I reviewed the 18% increase and wanted to talk through it before we move forward.

We've been a steady customer for the past three years, and this jump is well above the 5-7% range we've seen across our other vendors. Could you share what's driving the increase? If it's tied to raw materials, I'd love to explore whether locking in a 12-month volume commitment on our end could help you bring the rate closer to 8-10%.

I value our partnership and want to find a solution that keeps us moving forward together.

Best,
Diana

final_entries.prompt: I just started a new role and want to ask for an extra week of PTO in my first-year package.
final_entries.response:
Subject: Quick Question About First-Year PTO

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the warm onboarding — I'm really enjoying getting up to speed on the team.

I wanted to ask about the vacation allocation for my first year. The offer mentions two weeks, which I understand is the standard policy. Because I'll be wrapping up several personal commitments this fall, would there be any flexibility to add a third week to my first-year balance? I'd be happy to discuss how we can schedule it so coverage isn't impacted.

Either way, I'm thrilled to be here and excited about the work ahead.

Best,
Carlos

final_entries.prompt: I've been working with a freelance client for 18 months. Help me raise my rate for next quarter.
final_entries.response:
Subject: Rate Adjustment for Q1

Hi Priya,

It's been great partnering with you over the past year and a half. I'm writing to share a quick update on my rates going forward.

Starting next quarter, my project rate will be moving from $85/hr to $100/hr. This change reflects the expanded scope we've taken on (you'll notice I've been handling both the content audits and the CMS migrations now) and the additional turnaround SLA we agreed to in October.

For existing projects already in progress, there's no change — this only applies to new work scoped after December 31. If you'd like, we can also discuss a small discount for committing to a 3-month block upfront.

Let me know what you think.

Thanks,
Nina

final_entries.prompt: Write a Slack message to my manager about splitting the client presentation prep between two of us instead of doing it solo.
final_entries.response:
Hey Maya 👋

Quick heads-up — the client deck for Thursday is shaping up to be bigger than expected (roughly 20 slides with the new data section). Would it make sense to split the prep between us? I can own the market analysis and competitive slides, and you could take the case studies and financials. That way we both have something to polish over the weekend instead of one person carrying the full load.

Totally happy to adjust if you've already got another plan, but thought it was worth flagging early.

Thanks!

final_entries.prompt: I bought a laptop stand from an online vendor and it arrived cracked. I want a full refund plus they should cover return shipping. Draft a firm but polite email.
final_entries.response:
Subject: Defective Item — Order #48291 — Return & Refund Request

Hi,

I received my order (#48291) yesterday and unfortunately the laptop stand arrived with a crack across the base. I've attached a photo for reference.

Since the item was damaged in transit, I'd like to request a full refund of $49.99. Could you also please provide a prepaid return label so I don't have to absorb the shipping cost for a product that wasn't delivered as expected?

I've been a loyal customer and have always had good experiences, so I appreciate your help getting this sorted quickly. Please let me know the next steps.

Best regards,
Trevor
